CRM.thesis_one_line: The world's #1 CRM software leader, cheaply priced, but recently borrowed $25 billion to buy back stock and is increasingly growing through acquisitions.
kill_criteria: Reported revenue growth (GAAP, total) falls below 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Net debt/TTM operating cash flow rises above 2.5x (from ~1.8x currently) without a disclosed plan to delever.
The Contentful or Fin acquisition fails to close by 2026-12-31, or closes with a materially adverse regulatory condition disclosed in an 8-K.
GAAP operating margin guidance is cut a third consecutive time (below the current 20.1% FY27 guide).
cRPO growth (constant currency) falls below 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters - the earliest read on a genuine organic demand slowdown.
key_adverse_facts: Total debt rose 2.7x in six months (~$14.4bn to $39.3bn; noncurrent debt ~$10.4bn to $39.3bn) to fund a $25bn debt-financed accelerated share repurchase; stockholders' equity fell from $59.1bn to $38.4bn over the same period. [DV11 2026-10-06: earlier text said gross debt quadrupled.]
OCF/FCF growth guidance was cut in half (from ~9-10% to ~4-5%) explicitly because of the debt-service cost of the buyback, per management's own 1Q FY27 release.

Reported revenue growth is increasingly inorganic: Informatica contributed 4.5 points of 2Q FY27's ~11% growth (organic about 6%), with two more cash-funded acquisitions (Contentful $1.5bn, Fin $3.6bn) pending. [Corrected 2026-10-06, DVH4]
GAAP operating margin guidance has been cut twice in a row this fiscal year (20.9% to 20.6% to 20.1%) even as non-GAAP margin guidance held flat at 34.3%.
data_conflicts: This dossier's FCF-based reverse DCF (~1%/yr implied growth) differs in magnitude from V1's growth-based implied-growth figure (13.0%), though both conclude the stock is priced below a reasonable base case; the gap is attributed to TTM FCF being elevated by favorable working-capital timing in the always-large fiscal Q1.

b1_live_scores.csv's strong SUE/FCF-yield percentiles partly reflect the 2Q FY27 EPS surge (GAAP +119% YoY), which came mainly from a $2.6bn strategic-investment gain ($2.43/share), not from the buyback or organic momentum. [Corrected 2026-10-06, DVH4]
CRM.confidence_in_thesis: medium: the core SaaS franchise, cRPO acceleration and cheap reverse-DCF valuation are well evidenced by primary sources, but confidence is capped by the very recent, large increase in leverage and the rising share of growth coming from M&A rather than organic execution.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's growth-based reverse DCF (implied 13.0% vs consensus 9.7%) and this dossier's own FCF-based reverse DCF use different methods but reach the same conclusion - priced below a reasonable base case; this analyst is more cautious than V1 on the quality of that growth (increasingly M&A-driven) and the new leverage, hence INCLUDE-SMALL rather than full INCLUDE. [DV11 2026-10-06: restated at a 10.15% cost of equity and FCF after $3.7bn SBC, implied growth about 5.1%/yr, not ~1%.] [DVH4 2026-10-06: on the programme Blume beta Ke is 9.87% and implied growth about 4.5%/yr, equal to the FY27 FCF growth guide of 4-5%; the EPS used in V1's 14.4x NTM P/E and in the scenarios includes about $2.98/share of one-off strategic-investment gains (clean multiple about 17x); scenarios restated to bear -10.2%, base +5.0%, bull +18.7%; implied_vs_base unchanged (below) but supported by the FCF method only.]

CRM.scenario_basis: DVH4 2026-10-06 restated: start EPS = clean FY27 non-GAAP EPS $13.71 (guide midpoint $16.69 less $2.98 per share of H1 strategic-investment gains that the non-GAAP measure does not exclude); start P/E 17.1x at $234.02; bear = 3%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 11x and 0.8% avg dividend yield; base = 10%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 14.5x and 0.8% yield; bull = 16%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 18x and 0.6% yield; all over a 3-year horizon. Previous values on $16.69: bear -4.2%, base +12.0%, bull +26.7%.

CSCO.thesis_one_line: The dominant computer-networking company riding an AI data-center building boom, but the stock already prices in that boom lasting a decade.
kill_criteria: Quarterly revenue growth (GAAP, YoY) decelerates below 8% for two consecutive quarters (from +17.6% in Q4 FY26) - the clearest signal the AI-order cycle is normalizing faster than guided.
FY27 guidance (revenue $72.2-73.4bn or non-GAAP EPS $5.05-5.11) is cut at any quarterly update.
AI-infrastructure order intake (as separately disclosed by the company) declines sequentially for two consecutive quarters.

Net debt/TTM FCF rises above 2.0x (currently ~1.07x on total debt $29.5bn less cash and investments $15.9bn; ~1.75x on debt less cash only) without a corresponding disclosed reason (e.g., a large acquisition). [DV11 2026-10-06: corrected from ~1.2x]
Non-GAAP operating margin (currently guided 35.5-36.5% for Q1 FY27) compresses more than 200 bps YoY for two consecutive quarters.
key_adverse_facts: FY27 guidance (initial) implies a large step-up to +14-16% revenue growth, predicated on AI-infrastructure revenue nearly doubling ($4bn to $7.5bn) from a concentrated, lumpy hyperscaler order book.
The forward P/E has re-rated from Cisco's historical mid-teens range to ~19-20x alongside the AI-networking narrative, leaving little room for a guidance miss.
A longstanding Brazilian import-tax dispute carries undiscounted claims of $153M tax, $969M interest and $315M penalties (disputed, believed without merit, but not yet resolved after two decades).
A restructuring plan announced May 2026 is still being executed through FY27, a recurring GAAP-vs-non-GAAP reconciling cost.
data_conflicts: This dossier's own TTM FCF-yield calculation (~3.0%) does not exactly match d4_live_snapshot.parquet's fcf_yield field (2.66%), likely a capex/lease-capitalization definitional difference; it does not change the valuation conclusion.
CSCO.confidence_in_thesis: high: the beat-and-raise pattern (3 for 3 across FY26, with exact quoted guidance ranges) and revenue acceleration are unambiguous in primary sources; the main uncertainty is not whether the business is executing well right now but whether the AI-order cycle that is now priced in for a full decade will actually last that long.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CSCO in this run (not covered), so there is nothing to reconcile; this dossier's own reverse DCF (implied ~11.9%/yr FCF growth vs a base case of ~7-9%/yr, front-loaded then normalizing) independently supports an 'above base case' / not-cheap view, which is why the verdict is WATCH rather than INCLUDE despite excellent execution. [DV11 2026-10-06: with the 10-year Treasury at 5.17% the cost of equity is 10.13% (9.28% on a 4.14% ERP) and implied growth is 14.2% (12.2%), or 19.0% (16.9%) after $3.8bn SBC; implied_vs_base stays above.]

CSCO.scenario_basis: Non-GAAP diluted EPS $5.08 (FY27 guided midpoint); FY1 P/E ~19.0x start (NTM 20.4x); bear = 4%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 15x and 2.0% avg dividend yield; base = 10%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 18x and 1.8% yield; bull = 16%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 21x and 1.5% yield; all over a 3-year horizon.

EFX.thesis_one_line: A credit-bureau and employment-data company whose growth is reaccelerating and looks cheap, though regulators are still investigating its core data business.
kill_criteria: Consolidated revenue growth (GAAP, YoY) falls back below 5% for two consecutive quarters (from +10.6% in Q2 2026) - a signal the re-acceleration has stalled.
The CFPB investigation into Workforce Solutions results in a public enforcement action, consent order, or disclosed monetary penalty (currently: investigation ongoing, no action disclosed).
The FCRA class-action settlement (agreement in principle, June 2026) fails court approval, or the final settled/reserved amount exceeds $200M (from the $100M gross accrual booked in 2Q 2026).
Net debt/TTM FCF rises above 4.5x (from ~3.5x currently) without a corresponding disclosed reason.
Full-year Adjusted EPS guidance (currently $8.39-8.69 for FY2026) is cut at any quarterly update - a break from the 'beat-but-hold' pattern in the opposite (negative) direction.
key_adverse_facts: CFPB has been investigating Workforce Solutions' FCRA compliance and data accuracy since July 2023 (three CIDs through August 2024), with no resolution disclosed as of the 2026-07-21 10-Q.
A $100M accrual (net $40M after a $60M insurance receivable) was booked in 2Q 2026 for a not-yet-court-approved settlement of the 2022 FCRA coding-issue class action.
A separate antitrust class action (filed May 2024) alleges anticompetitive conduct specifically in the Workforce Solutions verification market, unresolved.
Net debt/TTM FCF is approximately 3.5x, and the cash balance ($170M) is thin relative to a $17.4bn market cap, though backstopped by an undrawn revolving credit facility.
data_conflicts: b1_live_scores.csv shows deeply negative 12-month momentum (-25.4%, 3.8th percentile) and weak SUE despite the company beating guidance in 8 of the last 8 reported quarters per d4_live_snapshot.parquet - this dossier attributes the gap to the open regulatory/legal overhang and macro mortgage-cycle uncertainty rather than a fundamental problem, but flags it as unresolved tension between price action and fundamentals.
This dossier's own TTM FCF-yield calculation (~6.35%) does not exactly match d4_live_snapshot.parquet's fcf_yield field (5.45%), likely a capex-definition difference.
EFX.confidence_in_thesis: medium: revenue re-acceleration and a cheap reverse-DCF valuation are well evidenced by primary sources, but confidence is capped by the unresolved CFPB investigation into the exact business unit (Workforce Solutions) that underpins the moat thesis.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for EFX in this run (not covered), so there is nothing to reconcile; this dossier's own reverse DCF (implied ~5.3%/yr FCF growth vs a base case of ~8-10%/yr) independently supports a 'cheap' view, tempered by the CFPB/legal reservation that keeps the verdict at INCLUDE-SMALL rather than INCLUDE.

EFX.scenario_basis: Adjusted EPS $8.54 (FY2026 guided midpoint); FY1 P/E ~14.6x start (NTM 15.2x); bear = 3%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 13x and 1.8% avg dividend yield; base = 10%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 16x and 1.6% yield; bull = 15%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 19x and 1.4% yield; all over a 3-year horizon.
